title: Captured frames are written to the DB with NO gain, offset, sensor temperature, mount pointing, focuser position or target link - although the FITS file it just wrote has all of them
summary: Split in two, and only half was still open. (a) The capture-truth columns were already closed in the working tree: the frame event now carries the Rust FrameContext's own values (native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/event.rs:981 FrameCaptureMetadata -> packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/ffi_backend/event_mapping.dart:558,576 -> event_operations.dart:638 FrameCapture.fromEventData -> images_dao.dart:761-808 which now lists sensor_temp, cooler_power, mount_ra/dec/altitude/azimuth, pier_side, focuser_position, focuser_temp, rotator_angle in its INSERT), and gain/offset come from the camera's report with the tree walk only as a legacy-host fallback (event_operations.dart:791-792). I proved it against the verifier's own scratch DB: /tmp/ns-audit/v2-sequencer-run/data/skotiq.db has gain=100, offset=10, sensor_temp=15.0, mount_ra=0.0, focuser_position=25070 on every captured_images row - the report's own NULL list was stale for those columns. (b) target_id was genuinely still NULL, and that half had no test at all: the `targets` table was EMPTY after three complete runs in that same DB, so every frame was filed as Untargeted. _bindCatalogTargets (sequence_executor.dart:687) gives each builder-authored TargetHeader a targets row at run start and _runTargetIdFor resolves it per frame, but it was only wired into start(); a RESUMED run bound nothing, so post-crash frames kept landing with target_id NULL. Wired it into the resume path too (sequence_executor.dart:1995) and put the whole path under test.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/resume_session_identity_test.dart - 'a fresh run binds its builder-authored target too' and 'frames captured after a resume are attributed to their target' drive the real executor.start()/resumeFromCheckpoint(), push a FrameAccepted through handleSequencerEventForTest and assert the captured_images row's target_id resolves to the 'M31' targets row. Existing (kept green): test/providers/sequence/sequence_frame_capture_metadata_test.dart (5 tests) for the capture columns.
revert_check: Deleting `await _bindCatalogTargets(sequence);` (sequence_executor.dart:756) fails 'a fresh run binds its builder-authored target too' with Expected 'M31' Actual <null>; deleting `await _bindCatalogTargets(resumedSequence);` (sequence_executor.dart:1995) fails 'frames captured after a resume are attributed to their target' the same way. Both restored and re-run green.
caveats: The capture-metadata half is pre-existing uncommitted work from an earlier wave; I verified it end to end rather than re-doing it. A target with an empty name still records target_id NULL by design - inventing a library entry called "" would be worse.

title: The Continue Session handoff dialog says 'Unknown Profile' and 'No Sequence' while naming the sequence in its own header and with a real profile active
summary: The verifier's upstream diagnosis was right (imaging_sessions rows carried profile_id/sequence_id NULL) and half-fixed in the tree: _startSessionRow now passes both on the fresh-start path (sequence_executor.dart:600-611). Two holes were left, and I found the decisive evidence in the verifier's own DB (/tmp/ns-audit/v2-sequencer-run/data/skotiq.db): the `sequences` table was EMPTY after three runs. (1) A sequence built in the sequencer and started without a trip through Save carries databaseId == null, so sequence_id would STILL be NULL and the dialog would still print 'No Sequence' - the run wrote a sequence_runs row named 'New Sequence' and no sequences row for it to point at. New _ensureSequencePersisted (sequence_executor.dart:637) saves an operator-authored plan before the run and has the editor adopt the id, so the session, the run row and the dialog all name the same real row; automated planners (autopilot/Smart Night/mosaic) are excluded so a night of generated trees does not bury the library. (2) The resume path called startSession(targetName:) only, dropping both ids on the one path the dialog exists for - an interrupted night. It now passes profileId and the recovered sequence's databaseId (sequence_executor.dart:1998-2002).
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/resume_session_identity_test.dart - 'a resumed run records its profile and its sequence', 'running a never-saved sequence still records which sequence ran' (asserts the sequences row exists, the session points at it and the editor adopted the id), 'an autopilot-generated run does not file itself in the library'. Existing (kept green): test/services/session_profile_sequence_binding_test.dart, whose 'the handoff context names the profile and the sequence' asserts QuickStartContext.profileName/sequenceName are non-null - the exact values the dialog renders.
revert_check: Replacing the resume-path call with `await sessionNotifier.startSession(targetName: info.sequenceName);` fails 'a resumed run records its profile and its sequence' (Expected <1> Actual <null>). Deleting `sequence = await _ensureSequencePersisted(sequence);` (sequence_executor.dart:734) fails 'running a never-saved sequence still records which sequence ran' (Expected length <1>, Actual []). Both restored and re-run green.
caveats: Sessions already in an existing database keep their NULLs - the profile and sequence that ran are not recoverable after the fact. Auto-persisting an operator's unsaved plan on run is a deliberate product change: a sequence you actually ran now appears in the library (that is what makes it reloadable).

title: 'Load Previous Setup' is inert: it restores no equipment, no sequence and writes nothing to the log - it just closes the dialog
summary: The verifier's sharpening was right: it is a false-success claim, not a dead button, and the reason it restored nothing was that the session row it was restoring FROM was empty. The tree already had the disclosure half (quick_start_dialog.dart:394 _hasRestorableSetup disables the primary and prints why; quick_start_checker.dart:268-347 reports what was actually applied instead of an unconditional 'Loaded previous setup ... from frame 1'). That is a message, not a fix - so I closed the cause: `imaging_sessions.equipment_snapshot` had a schema column, a reader (QuickStartService._buildQuickStartContext) and a restore path (QuickStartChecker._applyEquipmentSnapshot) and NO writer anywhere in the app - captureEquipmentSnapshot/saveEquipmentSnapshot had zero production callers, and the verifier's DB confirms it (equipment_snapshot NULL on all three sessions). SessionStateNotifier.startSession now stamps the live camera/filter/focuser state onto the row it just opened (session_provider.dart:207 + _recordEquipmentSnapshot), routed through the new ImagingRecordsRepository.updateEquipmentSnapshot so a paired companion does not write the phone's device state onto a host row. With profile_id and sequence_id also now recorded (see the previous item), the button re-activates the profile, re-opens the sequence and re-applies the cooler setpoint/gain/offset/filter/focuser it names.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/session_equipment_snapshot_test.dart - 'starting a session records the equipment it is running with' (asserts the persisted column parses back to gain 250 / offset 33 / bin 2x2 / 180 s) and 'the handoff context can offer that equipment back' (asserts QuickStartContext.hasEquipmentSnapshot, the flag the dialog gates the button on). packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/quick_start_checker_authority_test.dart - 'start fresh re-applies the recorded camera settings' taps the real button in the real QuickStartChecker and asserts exposureSettingsProvider.gain/offset and cameraStateProvider.targetTemp actually changed, not just the snackbar text.
revert_check: Deleting `await _recordEquipmentSnapshot(dbId);` (session_provider.dart:207) fails both session_equipment_snapshot_test tests (equipment_snapshot Expected not null, Actual <null>; hasEquipmentSnapshot Expected true, Actual false). Restored and re-run green.
caveats: The snapshot is taken at session START, not at end: a night that ends in a crash is exactly the night this dialog exists for, and an end-of-session read would come off equipment that may already be disconnected. Gain/offset/binning fall back to the configured capture settings when the driver does not read them back. 'Load Previous Setup' still does not CONNECT equipment - it loads the profile, the sequence and the capture settings, which is what it says.
